title: Test method for de-icing salt-frost scaling in high-performance concrete
author: Strand, Fridh
materials: The samples were placed inside a freezer (CF-A700, Kylcity, Skogås, Sweden). Each freezer had seven shelves and nine samples were placed on each shelf. The samples were then exposed to a pre-defined temperature cycle in which the air inside the freezers was maintained at −22 °C for 12 h and +22 °C for 12 h. Fig. 3 presents the temperature cycle, both in the salt solution and in air. It was important to always measure the temperatures inside the freezer and inside at least one cup in each freezer with a known position of the thermocouple. For additional information regarding the temperature cycle, see section ‘2.2 Methodical aspects – Temperature cycle’.Fig. 3Temperature cycle measured in the air inside a freezer and in the salt solution in a cup.Fig. 3

steps.title: Cast and saw concrete cylinders
steps.instruction: Cast concrete cylinders 200 mm long and 100 mm diameter; after curing, saw each cylinder into four samples of approximately 49 mm length and 100 mm diameter, and test only the sawed surfaces.

steps.title: Internal curing of cylinders
steps.instruction: Cure the cylinders in their moulds for 24 ± 2 h, demould, submerge them in lime‑saturated tap water for 7 days, then store them in plastic bags until they are sawn.

steps.title: Seal sample sides with rubber
steps.instruction: During the drying‑and‑carbonation (DaC) period (or during internal curing if no DaC), remove the cylinders from the bags for about 1 h to dry, then fasten a 330 ± 1 mm × 40 ± 1 mm EPDM rubber sheet (3 mm thick) to the sample sides with a silyl‑modified polymer adhesive (Xtreme Fix, Casco, Sika Sverige AB). Leave a narrow adhesive strip where the saw cut will be to avoid cutting the rubber. Return the samples to the bags (or directly to water for RS if no DaC).

steps.title: Drying and carbonation preconditioning
steps.instruction: Expose the sawed sample surfaces to +20 ± 0.5 °C, 60 ± 2 % relative humidity and approximately 400 ppm CO₂ for the prescribed DaC duration.

steps.title: Resaturation before testing
steps.instruction: Before the scaling test, expose the test surfaces to tap water for the resaturation (RS) period.

steps.title: Assemble insulation mould and distance aid
steps.instruction: Glue two pieces of extruded‑polystyrene insulation (XES 300 j, Paroc AB) together; drill a Ø 105 mm hole in the bottom piece. The combined diameter of sample, adhesive and rubber sheet is 106 mm, allowing it to be pressed into the mould. Place a 150 mm × 150 mm distance aid (thickness 10 mm, central Ø 120 mm hole) on the bench, insert the concrete sample so the test surface contacts the table, then press the insulation mould onto the sample until it contacts the distance aid, positioning the test surface 2 mm below the cup rim (i.e., 10 mm from the mould).

steps.title: Prepare 3 % NaCl solution and fill cups
steps.instruction: Mix 4850 g deionised water with 150 g 99.9 % NaCl (Falksalt) to obtain a 3 mass % NaCl solution. Cut a cup from the bottom of a polypropylene jar (S Unipac Square, Nordic Pack), fill each cup with 100 ± 1 ml of the solution using a 100 ml plastic syringe, and place the assembled insulation mould with concrete sample on top of the cup.

steps.title: Load samples into freezer and cycle
steps.instruction: Insert the cups (nine per shelf) onto the seven shelves of a CF‑A700 freezer (Kylcity). Run a freeze–thaw cycle of –22 °C for 12 h followed by +22 °C for 12 h, continuously measuring air temperature inside the freezer and solution temperature in at least one cup with a thermocouple.

steps.title: Perform measurements every seventh cycle
steps.instruction: Every seventh freeze–thaw cycle: (a) prepare paper filters (Melitta Original 1 × 4 coffee filters) labeled with sample name and cycle number and a fresh batch of 3 % NaCl solution; (b) remove one freezer shelf and place its samples on a bench in the original order; (c) gently lift each sample from its cup, place it in an open tray, and verify that the test surface is still in contact with the solution (note any leakage); (d) pour the solution and any scaled material into the filter; (e) brush the test surface 15–25 times in four perpendicular directions with a paint brush (fewer strokes if scaling is low); (f) rinse the surface with tap water collected in a tray, then place the sample on a wet cellulose‑based cloth (Wettex) and wipe off all water from the surface and mould; (g) weigh the sample together with its insulation mould, rubber sheet and adhesive on a balance with 0.1 g resolution; (h) refill the cup with fresh 3 % NaCl solution, return the sample to its cup and reposition it on the same shelf location; (i) pour the tray‑collected material into the same filter; (j) dry the filter at 105 ± 5 °C until the mass change is less than 0.001 g; (k) determine the dry mass of the scaled‑off concrete on a balance with 0.001 g resolution and subtract the filter mass.
